findings.bound_command: Confirmed. 29 assertions (15 card + 14 handler), registry_spec v2.4, exit 0, twice, and the two runs differ only in run-naming fields. The receipt's agreement claim is true as measured by me.
findings.routing_deviation_judgement: ACCEPTABLE INCREMENT, with a plan defect filed separately. The deviation's factual basis is fully reproduced: the declared key resolves to W17-01's program, that program reads no environment and therefore cannot route on check-id, tests/security/** is writable by no W09 card, and the declared argv refuses with zero assertions under BOTH v2.4 and v2.0 resolution. Appending W09-02 to that key would indeed have answered a W09 dispatch with W17's 148-id host roster: the dispatcher checks only that the supplied selectors are members of the key's lists, so adding W09/W09-02 to the lists is all it would take to make dispatch run a program that never hears the selector. That is a fabricated PASS and the executor declined it. The card's own binding clause - 'W02 registers this exact selector and real handler before use; UNBOUND/zero assertions is not PASS' - is satisfied in substance by a real in-scope handler bound to the exact selector; the deviation is the key NAME, the registrant, and the fact that the plan's declared argv is now a dead command.
findings.plan_defect: Real and line-level, not card-level: test.security means the W09 revocation gate in execution/commands.json (task W09, check W09-G02, cases A06/C02/C22 -> ops/ci/retrieval.py) but means W17-01's host-boundary program in execution/v2.4/commands.json. The plan's per-card argv was never re-pointed after that name was taken. W09-99 declares the same unresolvable pair (test.security --task-id W09 --check-id W09-G02 and --case-id A06), so it will hit this wall again, as will every card that declares a key whose handler sits outside its scope.
findings.hard_link_finding: Confirmed as fact and judged NOT blocking for this slice. Reproduced: a hard link inside a registered root is sealed and its bytes served, with content_hash equal to the outside file's digest. It is not one of the card's five named classes, the row is a characterisation that goes red the day it is closed, and nothing is leaked that the sealing OWNER could not already read - the root is registered by the same principal that can create the link. It is a genuine containment gap for any future model where a root is sealed for another party's files or where directory ACLs are the boundary, and it must be carried as an open obligation. Important correction to the receipt's framing: this one is fixable inside this card's own file, unlike the collapse gap - adapters/retrieval/identity_windows.go already calls syscall.GetFileInformationByHandle, whose ByHandleFileInformation carries NumberOfLinks.
findings.characterisation_rows_legitimacy: Legitimate in principle, mixed in practice. Two of the four are properly falsifiable: the collapse row t.Fatalf's when the two refusals stop being identical, and the hard-link row t.Fatalf's when the product starts refusing - I verified both go red under mutation (V06 kills 8 rows including the collapse row). The index row is the weakest: it only requires backend_revision to be non-empty, so it stays green if the value becomes scan-v1 (bounded-scan) and it never asserts the literal fts5-v1 the receipt quotes - it discloses, but cannot detect. The permission row is not legitimate at all: see problems P-1.
findings.per_leg_guard: It did not bind as described. Its constant_over_disjunction only fires when the replacement text literally contains '&& false' or '|| true' AND the anchor has more than one '&&'/'||' - so (a) it is blind to Python and/or compounds, which is why the executor's own M12 (whole condition 'version.returncode != 0 or ... != version_output' replaced by 'if False:') was executed, recorded as operands_anchor 0 / operands_replacement 0, and never refused: that IS a compound flip collapsing two decisions at once; (b) my V06 (Go '!IsRegular() && !IsDir()' replaced by 'if false {') is a two-operand collapse the guard also would not refuse (I ran their function on my pairs: guard_would_refuse=False for all 12). The rows' operands_anchor/operands_replacement fields are therefore not evidence of per-leg discipline. The conclusions survived anyway - all six of their 'caught' rows are genuinely caught (I reproduce the mechanism in V05b/V06/V07/V08/V10a) - so the misstatement is about the bookkeeping, not about the outcome.
findings.both_toolchain_legs_pair: I ran the pair the executor did not. With the digest leg AND the version leg both blinded, W0902-TOOLCHAIN-REFUSES-A-REAL-BUT-WRONG-BINARY goes red (failed_ids = that row plus HARNESS-ROSTER-EXACT). So the row is a live guard and does prove something: the decoy (python.exe as RESEARCHOS_GO) is refused, and it stops being refused only when both legs are gone. The named limitation resolves in the card's favour.
findings.class_witness_row: Live, contrary to the executor's own disclosure that its discriminating power was unproven. My V10a (CLASS_ROWS path_escape names a row the roster never emits) turns W0902-EVERY-NEGATIVE-CLASS-HAS-ITS-OWN-WITNESS red on its own; V10b (same bad input with the absence operand deleted) survives, which pins the killing power on exactly that operand. M11's survival is therefore benign.
findings.link_class_constructibility: The link class is witnessed by a construction a reviewer can actually build. I created a junction with cmd /c mklink /J (no privilege needed) and confirmed os.Root reports it with an irregular mode - the row's refusal text in my run reads 'path component "junction_dir" is a link or reparse point with irregular mode ?rw-rw-rw-'. os.Symlink fails with WinError 1314, so the ModeSymlink branch is genuinely unexamined ground (my compile-clean V05 redo survives), and a hard link is constructible (my own os.link, st_nlink 2).
findings.counterexample_reach: Deliverable 2's counter-example is witnessed for two of its three surfaces: the search surface refuses/omits and the sealed-body read returns 409 with the marker appearing 0 times (both reproduced from my own run's evidence payloads). The event/journal half is not reached, and I judge that alone does NOT block: the outbox event record built by internal/domain/store.go:336 carries only aggregate_ref, event_type, actor and correlation - event_data_artifact_ref is nil - so the journal cannot itself echo sealed bytes; a client replaying events must still dereference the artifact, which is exactly the path W0902-DELETED-SOURCE-SEALED-BODY-READ-IS-REFUSED and accepted W09-01's revoked-idempotent-replay row already gate. The half that is genuinely untried is 'an assembly made before the loss' - see problems P-4, where it was reachable.
findings.source_kind_placement: Right place for the wrong reason. The field makes the aggregate self-consistent with the stored Evidence and my V07 proves the row is live (deleting the key from the record literal goes red on 6 rows). But no client reads it from there: no HTTP route exposes EvidenceSupportSummary (internal/domain/http.go's method list has none), its only non-test consumer is candidates.go:134 which reads independent_observed_count for the ADOPT gate, and apps/web already renders source_kind from the Evidence row (screens.jsx evidence list/detail, plus cycle.source_coverage) - which accepted W09-01 covers with W0901-EVIDENCE-ROW-CARRIES-LOCATOR-TYPE-OBSERVED-AT-AND-SNAPSHOT-REF. So it is not cosmetic, but it is also not the CLI/Desktop projection action 3 asks for.

problems.title: W0902-PERMISSION-LEG-CANNOT-BE-ISOLATED-AT-THE-SEARCH-SURFACE asserts a premise I disproved
problems.detail: The row and not_covered item 4 both state that a second principal with equal roles and equal grants sees zero hits, so the key cannot be shown to move on permission alone. In the card's own sequence the snapshot had ALREADY been made stale and already produced zero hits one step earlier (the row's own evidence records hits_after=0 for the previous step), so the observation is inherited, not caused by the principal change. My probe P2 built the clean construction - one fresh CURRENT snapshot, same project, same state revision (5 = 5), same manifest, second principal w0902_review_reader with a project grant - and measured owner_hits=1, second_hits=1, owner_hash 8f63d3f0... != second_hash 44c6263d..., warnings empty. The permission leg IS isolable at the search surface and DOES move the key; the row is a passing roster entry carrying a false factual claim.
problems.required_action: Replace the row with the positive isolation witness (rename to e.g. W0902-PERMISSION-LEG-MOVES-WITH-PRINCIPAL-ALONE, before/after hashes plus equal state revision and equal hits), and delete not_covered item 4. The probe I used is recorded verbatim in _reviewer_scratch_r1/reviewer_probes_round1.json.

problems.title: The source-leg row does not vary one leg and the actions_map claim that it does is false
problems.detail: W0902-KEY-CHANGES-WHEN-SEALED-CONTENT-CHANGES records varied:'source bytes only' and hits_after:0. My probe P3 measured the same step: ProjectState revision moved 5 -> 7 across RefreshLocalSnapshots and the snapshot left the manifest (hits 1 -> 0), while a later byte change with no refresh at all did NOT move the key relative to the post-refresh hash. The key is Hash([project, state_revision, grantHash, retrievalRevision, manifest]); live file bytes are not a component - a content change invalidates by excluding the snapshot, and the state revision moves with it. So two other components moved in the same step. The invalidation behaviour the card actually needs is real (old bytes were never served, marker never echoed - I reproduce both), but the receipt's sentence 'each runtime-varied leg was tested on its own' and the row's 'varied: source bytes only' are not true, and the project leg is never varied by any row at all.

problems.title: Three containment legs/branches are asserted by nothing, and one row name over-claims
problems.detail: My V03 removes the '!filepath.IsLocal(relative)' operand entirely and all 29 assertions still PASS - os.Root refuses the escape anyway, so no row can tell the pre-check is gone. Consequently W0902-LEXICAL-ESCAPE-REFUSED-BEFORE-THE-ROOT-IS-OPENED, whose logged evidence is the domain's collapsed 'GATE_FAILED: root-scoped file unavailable', evidences neither 'before the root is opened' nor 'lexical'. My V04 replaces classifyOpen's intermediate-component branch ('could not be inspected') with the generic message and all 29 still PASS, though the branch is reachable (any path whose parent directory is absent). My compile-clean V05 redo of the ModeSymlink branch survives: host-unreachable ground. The executor's M03 'caught' does not cover V03's case - negating the operand makes the guard refuse everything, which is an over-refusal signal, not a witness of the containment leg.

problems.title: not_covered item 1's stated reason is contradicted by a green pre-existing test in the same package
problems.detail: The receipt says the ContextBundle call site is unreachable because 'a task needs the accepted-requirement chain ... a bare fixture requirement answers POST /tasks with 400 CreateTaskRequest schema (measured, not assumed)'. TestW09A06HTTPInvalidationAndContext in internal/domain/retrieval_test.go already does exactly that with f.requirement(), f.task(), f.bundle() and MaterializeTaskContext before and after the source changes, and I ran it green (ok, 0.878s) together with TestW09RootReplacementCannotFeedProduct and TestW09TaskInputCannotRematerializeStaleLocalBody. The helpers exist and the path is reachable from this card's own test file. The disclosure is conservative (it under-claims rather than over-claims) and the substance is witnessed by another card's tests, but the stated justification is wrong and the assembly half was not in fact blocked.

The permission leg is isolable at the search surface; this row must be replaced by the positive isolation witness before W09-99 relies on it.

L-2 (must be restated verbatim): W0902-KEY-CHANGES-WHEN-SEALED-CONTENT-CHANGES does not vary the source leg alone - RefreshLocalSnapshots moved the ProjectState revision 5 -> 7 and dropped the snapshot from the manifest in the same step (reviewer probe P3). The invalidation itself is genuine (stale bytes never served); the receipt's 'each runtime-varied leg was tested on its own' and the row's 'varied: source bytes only' are withdrawn, and the project leg is untested by any row.

L-3 (must be restated verbatim): the lexical containment operand and two classifier branches are unasserted - removing '!filepath.IsLocal(relative)' leaves all 29 rows green (reviewer mutant V03), replacing classifyOpen's intermediate-component branch leaves all 29 green (V04), and the ModeSymlink branch is host-unreachable (compile-clean V05 survives). L-5 (must be restated verbatim): W0902-INDEX-LEG-IS-A-COMPILE-TIME-CONSTANT asserts only that backend_revision is non-empty; it never asserts fts5-v1 and stays green when the hit is served by the bounded-scan path (scan-v1). No HTTP route exposes EvidenceSupportSummary, its only non-test reader is the ADOPT gate in candidates.go which reads independent_observed_count, and apps/web renders source_kind from the Evidence record (covered by accepted W09-01) plus cycle.source_coverage (owned by the W16 flow). Not blocking this slice because it is outside the card's five named classes, the sealing principal already holds local read access, and the row fails loudly if it is ever closed - but it is an OPEN SECURITY OBLIGATION and its fix is available inside this card's own file (adapters/retrieval/identity_windows.go already reads ByHandleFileInformation, which carries NumberOfLinks).

The 'assembly made before the loss' half is witnessed by pre-existing green tests (TestW09A06HTTPInvalidationAndContext) and not by this card.

The append to execution/v2.4/commands.json (rev 21 -> 22) was self-registered by a card that does not own that file.
